answer: Rate limiting with subnet fingerprinting: each /24 IPv4 block gets a token bucket of 5 registrations/hour; excess requests are dropped, not queued. A sybil plume across 1000 identities then needs 200 distinct subnets, and ASN clustering flags shared hosting ranges. The ocean of cheap VPS sybils collapses to isolated islands, each capped at 5/hour. Cost per durable identity rises from ~$0.10 to ~$4 plus ASN diversity overhead. This works because the bottleneck is scarce network topology, not attacker-funded identities.
